title: Indian stroke speech corpus / Characterizing stroke-affected speech using F0 and duration-based features
task: five sustained vowels (each twice); three-word phonetically rich read sentences
token_or_recording_size: 50 stroke + 50 healthy speakers; five sustained vowels x2 per participant plus sentence recordings
annotation_target: manually segmented sustained-vowel utterances and sentence utterances; F0 contour statistics; automatically derived transition/steady-state timing features
manual_scope: raw audio manually segmented into independent vowel-category utterances; sentence recordings similarly segmented; transition-region boundaries themselves are algorithmic and must not be represented as manual
decision_reason: Primary Telugu clinical/control production corpus with explicit manual segmentation of the relevant recorded vowel and sentence utterances and a public Zenodo deposit.
evidence_summary: Scientific Reports methods state that raw audio was manually segmented into independent utterances for each vowel category and similarly for sentences. Corpus comprises 50 stroke patients and 50 healthy controls, all Telugu L1 speakers. Authors report F0 mean/median/SD and transition/non-transition duration-derived features; transition regions are automatically detected and should retain that provenance. Data availability identifies Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.15675906 / record 15675907.

title: Movement variability can be modulated in speech production
task: single-word reading with real-time F1/F2 auditory perturbation across four experiments
token_or_recording_size: Experiment Ns 24,22,21,20; experiments 1-3 use 40 baseline + 100 exposure + 40 washout trials per stimulus; three vowel words per experiment
annotation_target: F1/F2 productions; vowel onset/offset; production-error screening; perturbation phase/type; trial-level formant variability
manual_scope: vowel onset/offset initially detected by participant-specific amplitude thresholds and errors in automatically defined landmarks manually corrected using waveform and spectrogram; all trials manually checked for production errors
decision_reason: Primary controlled production data with public data/code and explicit exhaustive human checking/correction of vowel landmark errors; unusually high-value trial-level F1/F2 perturbation dataset.
evidence_summary: Paper reports 87 native American-English speakers across four experiments. F1/F2 were tracked offline; all trials were manually checked for production errors, vowel onset/offset were detected automatically and landmark errors manually corrected with waveform and spectrogram. Data and associated code are public at OSF STJC9.

title: AphasiaBD: A Bengali Speech Dataset for Broca's and Global Aphasia
token_or_recording_size: 335 segmented audio clips; Patient Data.zip 194.3 MB
annotation_target: sentence-level clip boundaries; task labels; aphasia diagnosis/group information
manual_scope: recordings manually segmented at sentence level
decision_reason: New primary Bengali clinical production corpus with explicit manual sentence-level segmentation and openly downloadable recordings; useful warehouse source even though no deposited acoustic measurements are advertised.
evidence_summary: Zenodo record published 2026-08-09 describes 38 post-stroke speakers with Broca's or Global Aphasia, 335 clips across conversation/repetition/question-answering/reading tasks, smartphone recordings in natural environments, and explicit manual sentence-level segmentation. Single 194.3 MB Patient Data.zip has MD5 c2b0b71f5599d0c2a0f64bd03ed9dcb0.

title: Dataset of audiovisual unscripted monologues with speech annotations
task: unscripted laboratory monologues on self-selected topics; babble-noise and visual-modification conditions
token_or_recording_size: more than 300 minutes; 60 takes; one 6.2 MB annotation ZIP linked to the original audiovisual corpus
annotation_target: word, phoneme and pause onsets/durations; orthography; XSAMPA phonetic and canonical representations; syllabification; POS and lemma
manual_scope: annotation pipeline used OCTRA/G2P/MAUS/PHO2SYL/RFTagger, with manual correction steps used to ensure transcription accuracy and improve forced-alignment quality; retain the corrected word/phoneme event layer and its automatic-plus-manual provenance
access: public Zenodo annotation layer plus public primary audiovisual corpus
decision_reason: Public 2026 annotation release links directly to the same project's six-speaker primary recordings and provides a separable manually corrected word/phoneme event layer suitable for future acoustic extraction without duplicating underlying recordings.
evidence_summary: Data in Brief article reports >300 min from six speakers across 60 takes and manual correction steps to improve transcription and forced alignment. Zenodo 17578693 provides event.tsv/JSON/HED annotations with word/phoneme/pause onset and duration plus XSAMPA and lexical fields, explicitly derived from primary audiovisual dataset Zenodo 8082844.

title: Open-Source Manually Annotated Vocal Tract Database for Automatic Segmentation from 3D MRI Using Deep Learning
task: static 3D vocal-tract configurations for phoneme production and voiceless tasks
token_or_recording_size: 53 manually annotated 3D vocal-tract volumes; 21 unique French phonemes + 3 voiceless tasks
annotation_target: 3D upper-airway/vocal-tract segmentation masks; source MRI volumes; expert/manual annotator labels; STAPLE consensus reference masks
manual_scope: 53 volumes manually annotated by an expert vocologist assisted by two graduate students in voice science; multiple segmentations combined with STAPLE to form reference labels
preexisting_database_dependency: DERIVED_ANNOTATION_LAYER_ON_PREEXISTING_PRIMARY_MRI; isolate only new manual segmentation layer
decision_reason: Genuinely new manual articulatory annotations are isolatable from the earlier primary French-speaker MRI corpus; the new layer is directly useful for phoneme-specific vocal-tract geometry and can be linked without double-counting the underlying speakers/scans.
evidence_summary: Journal of Voice study reports 53 vocal-tract volumes from 10 French speakers, covering 21 phonemes and 3 voiceless tasks, manually annotated by an expert vocologist and graduate students. Figshare releases training/testing MRI volumes and segmentation labels, with STAPLE consensus outputs for the test set, under MIT license.

title: GIRAFE: Glottal Imaging Dataset for Advanced Segmentation, Analysis, and Facilitative Playbacks Evaluation
task: sustained vowel phonation; some sequences include vocal onset
token_or_recording_size: 65 HSV recordings; 502 frames each; 32,630 images; 4000 fps; 256x256 color; Zenodo record ~918.1 GB current version
annotation_target: frame-level glottal-gap semantic segmentation masks; sustained-vowel phonation sequences; health/pathology labels where known; automatic model segmentations as separate derived layer
manual_scope: all recordings manually annotated by an expert with glottal-gap semantic segmentation masks
access: metadata/code public; Zenodo data files currently restricted/request access; GitHub code public
license: dataset CC-BY-NC-4.0 per Data in Brief; companion GitHub code MIT
decision_reason: Primary clinical/control voice-production imaging corpus with expert manual glottal-gap masks. Retain as a restricted-data metadata/lineage source and do not mirror imaging files; companion code is public but does not change dataset access rights.
evidence_summary: Data in Brief specifications report 65 HSV recordings from 50 native Spanish-speaking participants, sustained vowel phonation, 4000-fps acquisition, metadata in JSON/XLSX and annotations in PKL, with expert manual glottal-gap masks. The paper states CC BY-NC 4.0; the Zenodo record currently marks files restricted/request access, while companion GitHub code is MIT-licensed.

title: TaL: a synchronised multi-speaker corpus of ultrasound tongue imaging, audio, and lip videos
data_mode: ultrasound tongue imaging + lip video + acoustic speech
task: read, spontaneous, silent and calibration speech tasks
token_or_recording_size: TaL1 one professional speaker across six sessions + TaL80 81 speakers; about 24 h parallel data / 13.5 h speech; repository download ~49 GB + 498 GB
annotation_target: manual short-segment boundaries and transcriptions for long spontaneous utterances; synchronized waveform, ultrasound and lip-video streams
manual_scope: long spontaneous utterances were manually divided into shorter typically 5-10 s segments with start/end times and transcription; no claim that phone boundaries are manual
evidence_summary: Large primary synchronized articulatory/acoustic corpus with an explicit manually annotated temporal subset that can anchor source-faithful multimodal production analyses without treating unverified phone alignment as manual.
verified_date: UltraSuite documentation reports 82 native English speakers, synchronized waveform/ultrasound/lip video, and explicitly states that long spontaneous utterances were manually annotated into shorter typically 5-10 s segments with start/end times and transcription. Only this manually grounded subset is admitted as annotated core; raw synchronized data remain linked for derived measurements.

title: Manual and automatic labels for version 1.0 of UXTD, UXSSD, and UPX core data
data_mode: ultrasound tongue imaging + acoustic speech + clinical annotation
task: typically developing child speech and speech-therapy/assessment sessions
token_or_recording_size: UXTD 58 speakers; UXSSD 8; UPX 20; annotation deposit contains three ZIP archives plus README
annotation_target: manually revised speaker/word boundaries for UXTD/UXSSD reference subset; speech-language-therapist manual labels where available; automatic speaker/word/phone labels retained separately
manual_scope: UXTD/UXSSD reference labels were manually revised by a single annotator at speaker level for 60 utterances and word level for 199 utterances; provided phone labels are force-aligned and are NOT admitted as manual; SLT labels are manual where available, including UPX
license: CC-BY-4.0 metadata record; DataShare end-user licence also applies to download
decision_reason: Separately deposited manual annotation layer over primary UltraSuite child production recordings. Manual reference word/speaker boundaries and SLT labels can be isolated cleanly while automatic phone/word/speaker tiers remain outside the manually grounded core.
evidence_summary: UltraSuite documents UXTD=58, UXSSD=8, UPX=20 speakers. UXTD/UXSSD reference labels were manually revised at speaker and word level (60 and 199 utterances respectively); phone labels remain forced-aligned despite manual word constraints. DataShare DOI 10.7488/ds/2429 provides the three label ZIPs and README and explicitly distinguishes manual/reference/SLT labels from automatically derived tiers.
